review_output: {"summary":"The core design holds up. Tenant scope is checked in both the TS code and the trigger. Captures can't be updated or truncated, and can only be deleted when a parent (submission or metric version) is deleted. Unknown attribution stays NULL, there is no backfill, and the original visitor is kept on duplicate inserts. I found no BLOCKERs, but there are 7 MAJOR issues that should be fixed before the form HTTP code and the scheduler are built on this. (1) captureMetricRegistration runs inside the caller's submission transaction with no savepoint. Any SQL error (trigger RAISE, foreign-key failure, timeout) aborts the whole Postgres transaction, so a metric problem fails the visitor's registration. (2) materializeMetricRegistration returns \"source_unavailable\" both when it should retry and when it never can succeed. \"Keep coverage unknown until drained\" can then never finish. (3) The rule verifiedAt >= capturedAt compares two timestamps that may come from different clocks, so correct rows can be excluded forever. (4) verifiedAt passes through a JS Date before the insert, which can break the existing trigger's exact-epoch check. (5) A capture blocks deletion of its visitor and can never be changed or removed on its own, so erasing a visitor is impossible unless the whole submission or metric version is deleted. (6) The capture step uses clock_timestamp() at different moments, so near the expiry boundary it can fail with a SQL error instead of returning SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE. (7) A later verification change turns into a permanent IDENTITY_CONFLICT that looks like a retryable error. The 4 MINOR and 2 NIT findings cover lock ordering, error classification, hygiene and test coverage. I didn't penalize the unbuilt HTTP wiring or scheduler.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Transaction integrity / availability","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"Capture runs inside the caller's first FormSubmission transaction with no SAVEPOINT. A Postgres error from the capture step (guard-trigger RAISE 23514, foreign-key violation, statement timeout, deadlock) puts the whole transaction into an aborted state. The code turns it into PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE, but the caller can't catch that and carry on: the next statement fails with 25P02, so the submission itself rolls back.","evidence":"captureMetricRegistration(tx: Prisma.TransactionClient, ...) runs $queryRaw/$executeRaw directly on the caller's tx. The catch block only rewrites the JS error and can't undo the server-side abort. The trigger raises for 'metric capture collection unavailable' and 'initial submission unavailable'.","impact":"An optional metrics side-write can block real user registrations. That includes every submission created with a status other than UNVERIFIED and any request that hits the expiry boundary (see the clock_timestamp finding).","recommended_fix":"Wrap the capture in SAVEPOINT metric_capture / RELEASE, and ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT on error. Make the function return a typed result such as { visitorId } | { status: 'unavailable', code }. Treat failures as 'no capture' (unknown attribution) and don't let them affect the submission.","required_test":"Integration test: create a submission in a transaction, force the capture trigger to raise (for example, set expiresAt to now() between the check and the insert, or set the status to VERIFIED), and assert that the submission still commits with no capture row.","confidence":0.85},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Correctness / race","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"The collection window is evaluated with clock_timestamp() at three moments: the TS SELECT, proofs.verify(nowAt), and the trigger's re-check. If expiresAt passes between the TS check and the INSERT, the trigger raises an SQL exception instead of the code returning SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE cleanly. With the previous finding, this aborts the registration.","evidence":"TS: \"expiresAt\">clock_timestamp() in the SELECT. Trigger: IF NOT EXISTS(... \"expiresAt\">clock_timestamp()) THEN RAISE.","impact":"Registrations submitted right at version expiry fail, and the failure is non-deterministic.","recommended_fix":"Keep the trigger as the authoritative guard, but run the insert under a savepoint and map a trigger 23514 to SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE. You could also pass a single nowAt into the trigger via a session GUC, or accept a small grace window in the trigger.","required_test":"Use a version with expiresAt a few milliseconds ahead, add a pg_sleep injection between the check and the insert, and assert that the result is SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE and the outer transaction stays usable.","confidence":0.7},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Reconciliation / coverage correctness","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"materializeMetricRegistration returns 'source_unavailable' both for 'not verified yet' (retry later) and for permanent ineligibility: verified at or after v.expiresAt, verifiedAt < capturedAt, Live.formId changed, submission REJECTED, and so on. The reconciler can't tell which captures are terminal.","evidence":"if (rows.length !== 1) return { status: \"source_unavailable\" as const }; follows a single combined JOIN/WHERE. The doc comment says 'keep coverage unknown until drained'.","impact":"A permanently ineligible capture stays in the queue forever. Coverage then never becomes known for that version (or the scheduler retries forever), which leaves reports stuck at unknown.","recommended_fix":"Split the check into separate statuses: 'pending_verification' (status UNVERIFIED), 'ineligible_expired', 'ineligible_scope_mismatch', 'ineligible_not_verified' (terminal), and so on. Have the reconciler drain on terminal statuses.","required_test":"Table-driven test covering a verified-after-expiry capture, a Live.formId change, a rejected submission and an unverified submission. Assert that each returns a different status, and that only the unverified case counts as non-drained.","confidence":0.8},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Data integrity / timestamps","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"Eligibility requires verifiedAt >= capturedAt. capturedAt always comes from the DB's clock_timestamp(), but FormSubmission.verifiedAt may be written by the app (new Date()) or with different precision. If the app clock runs behind the DB clock, or verifiedAt is truncated or rounded differently, a correctly ordered verification is excluded forever. The trigger already proves the order (it requires status = 'UNVERIFIED' at capture time), so this check adds nothing and only creates risk.","evidence":"AND (f.\"verifiedAt\" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')>=c.\"capturedAt\" plus the trigger check s.\"verificationStatus\"='UNVERIFIED'. Likewise, <=clock_timestamp() assumes the two clocks agree.","impact":"Some verified registrations silently never materialize, so the visitor-to-registration counts are undercounted.","recommended_fix":"Remove the verifiedAt >= capturedAt condition (ordering is already enforced by the UNVERIFIED guard), or require that verifiedAt is always set from the DB clock and document that. Keep only the expiresAt bound.","required_test":"Set verifiedAt to capturedAt minus 5 ms (simulating app clock skew) on a submission verified after capture, and assert that it materializes.","confidence":0.65},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Data integrity / exact epoch","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"verifiedAt makes a round trip through a JS Date (millisecond precision, and Prisma's raw-parameter timestamp typing) before it is inserted into LiveMetricRegistration. The existing trigger requires an exact verified epoch. If FormSubmission.verifiedAt has more than millisecond precision, or the session TimeZone isn't UTC when a timestamptz parameter is cast to a timestamp-without-time-zone column, the value won't match exactly. The trigger then raises, which becomes a retryable PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE on every replay.","evidence":"SELECT f.\"verifiedAt\" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS \"verifiedAt\" ... VALUES (..., ${source.verifiedAt}). The verify step then compares +registration.verifiedAt against +source.verifiedAt in JS.","impact":"Materialization can fail permanently with an error that looks transient.","recommended_fix":"Use INSERT INTO \"LiveMetricRegistration\" (...) SELECT ..., f.\"verifiedAt\" FROM ... with the same eligibility JOIN, so the value never leaves Postgres. Compare it in SQL as well (registration.\"verifiedAt\" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM f.\"verifiedAt\").","required_test":"Run with the session TimeZone set to something other than UTC and a microsecond-precision verifiedAt (if the schema allows it). Assert that materialization succeeds and the trigger accepts the exact epoch.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Data lifecycle / privacy erasure","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015100000_live_metric_registration_capture/migration.sql","issue":"The visitor foreign key is ON DELETE NO ACTION, the capture row can't be updated (the UPDATE guard also blocks any foreign-key SET NULL action), and it can only be deleted if its submission or version is gone. As a result, a single LiveMetricVisitor can never be deleted (erasure request, visitor-retention pruning) without deleting the whole FormSubmission or metric version.","evidence":"CONSTRAINT \"LiveMetricRegistrationCapture_visitor_fkey\" ... ON DELETE NO ACTION. The guard has IF TG_OP='UPDATE' THEN RAISE, and the DELETE branch raises while both parents exist.","impact":"Visitor deletion or retention jobs fail with a foreign-key violation, and there is no compliant way to remove one visitor's attribution.","recommended_fix":"Decide on a policy. One option is ON DELETE SET NULL (NULL means unknown, which matches the no-repair rule) with the guard allowing an UPDATE only when visitorId goes from non-NULL to NULL and every other column is unchanged. Alternatively, document and test the cascade path for visitor deletion. Apply the same policy to LiveMetricRegistration.","required_test":"Delete a LiveMetricVisitor that a capture references. Assert either that the capture's visitorId becomes NULL and the report is invalidated, or that the documented erasure procedure works.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Reconciliation / immutability semantics","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"If a submission's verifiedAt changes after it is first materialized (verification revoked and re-verified, or verifiedAt corrected), ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING keeps the old row and the verify step throws IDENTITY_CONFLICT on every replay. Callers will probably treat that like the other errors, but it is terminal.","evidence":"+registration.verifiedAt !== +source.verifiedAt leads to throw new MetricRegistrationError(\"IDENTITY_CONFLICT\").","impact":"The scheduler retries forever, or the capture is never drained. Reports may keep a stale verifiedAt.","recommended_fix":"Return a distinct terminal status (for example 'conflict') and record it, or make verifiedAt immutable on FormSubmission after the first verification. Document which applies.","required_test":"Materialize, then change FormSubmission.verifiedAt and materialize again. Assert that you get a deterministic terminal status and no retry loop.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Deadlocks / lock ordering","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"materializeMetricRegistration locks in the order LiveMetricVersion (SHARE), then Live (SHARE), then FormSubmission (SHARE). An admin path that updates Live first and then the version (for example, ending a live and disabling collection) acquires them in the opposite order, which can deadlock. The capture path also locks version before visitor while the caller already holds the FormSubmission row.","evidence":"Sequence of FOR SHARE statements on LiveMetricVersion, then Live, then FormSubmission. No lock_timeout is set.","impact":"Occasional 40P01 deadlocks, surfaced as PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE. These are recoverable through retry, but they create noise and latency.","recommended_fix":"Use one global lock order across all metric and verification paths (for example Live, then LiveMetricVersion, then FormSubmission, then Visitor, matching the existing verified-registration trigger). Set lock_timeout locally in both functions.","required_test":"Concurrency test: an admin transaction that updates Live and then LiveMetricVersion runs alongside materialize. Assert there is no deadlock, or a bounded retry.","confidence":0.45},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Error classification","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"Every Postgres error, including deterministic guard-trigger 23514 errors (scope unavailable, submission not UNVERIFIED) and foreign-key 23503 errors, becomes PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE. If proofs.verify throws on malformed input, that is also reported as a persistence error instead of unknown attribution.","evidence":"catch (error) { if (error instanceof MetricRegistrationError) throw error; throw new MetricRegistrationError(\"PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE\"); }. proofs.verify(proof, ...) is not wrapped.","impact":"Callers and the reconciler retry deterministic failures. Bad proofs can block capture when they should only degrade attribution to unknown.","recommended_fix":"Wrap proofs.verify in try/catch so any failure gives null. Map SQLSTATE 23514 and 23503 to SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE or IDENTITY_CONFLICT, and reserve PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE for connection, timeout and serialization errors.","required_test":"Pass a proof that makes verify throw and assert the capture is stored with visitorId=null. Force a trigger 23514 and assert a non-persistence error code.","confidence":0.7},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Idempotency","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015100000_live_metric_registration_capture/migration.sql","issue":"The BEFORE INSERT guard fires before ON CONFLICT is resolved. A repeat capture call after verification (status no longer UNVERIFIED), or after expiry, raises an error instead of DO NOTHING, so the TS ON CONFLICT/re-read idempotency path only works while the submission is still UNVERIFIED. The documentation does forbid repeat calls, but the code looks idempotent and isn't.","evidence":"INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (\"submissionId\") DO NOTHING versus the trigger's ... AND s.\"verificationStatus\"='UNVERIFIED' ... RAISE.","impact":"A repeat call from a retried request handler aborts the caller's transaction.","recommended_fix":"In TS, SELECT the existing capture first and return it before attempting the insert, or have the trigger skip its checks when a row with NEW.submissionId already exists.","required_test":"Capture, verify the submission, call capture again, and assert that the original visitorId comes back with no exception.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Capture availability","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"The capture step sets no statement or lock timeout. Its FOR SHARE on LiveMetricVersion waits behind any admin FOR UPDATE on that version for the full duration, which holds up the user's submission transaction.","evidence":"There is no set_config('statement_timeout'/'lock_timeout') in captureMetricRegistration, unlike materialize.","impact":"A long-running admin transaction on a version stalls public form submissions for that live.","recommended_fix":"Inside the savepoint, SET LOCAL lock_timeout to a short value (for example 500 ms) and treat a timeout as unknown or no capture.","required_test":"Hold FOR UPDATE on the version in another session. Assert that the capture gives up within the timeout and the submission still commits.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"NIT","area":"Indexes","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015100000_live_metric_registration_capture/migration.sql","issue":"The (vendorId, liveId, versionId) index is a left prefix of the (vendorId, liveId, versionId, visitorId) index, so it is redundant.","evidence":"CREATE INDEX ..._vendorId_liveId_versionId_idx and ..._scope_visitor_idx.","impact":"Extra write overhead and storage.","recommended_fix":"Drop the 3-column index. The 4-column index serves both foreign-key cascade lookups.","required_test":"EXPLAIN the version-delete cascade and the visitor-delete check, and confirm both use scope_visitor_idx.","confidence":0.8},{"severity":"NIT","area":"Migration / schema hygiene","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015100000_live_metric_registration_capture/migration.sql","issue":"The composite foreign keys depend on unique constraints on LiveMetricVersion(vendorId, liveId, id) and LiveMetricVisitor(vendorId, liveId, versionId, id), which this diff doesn't show. The matching Prisma model is also not shown, so `prisma migrate diff` may report drift.","evidence":"REFERENCES public.\"LiveMetricVersion\"(\"vendorId\",\"liveId\",id) and REFERENCES public.\"LiveMetricVisitor\"(\"vendorId\",\"liveId\",\"versionId\",id).","impact":"The migration fails if those unique constraints are missing. Schema drift could make a later generated migration drop the triggers or foreign keys.","recommended_fix":"Confirm the unique constraints exist in an earlier migration. Add the model to schema.prisma with @@unique and relations that match, and run a migrate diff check in CI.","required_test":"Apply migrations to an empty database and run prisma migrate diff --exit-code against schema.prisma.","confidence":0.4}]}
